literal: First year of Taiping Zhenjun, spring, first month, day jiyou: Juqu Wuhui besieged Jiuquan.
idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping Zhenjun, on the jiyou day of the first month of spring, Juqu Wuhui besieged Jiuquan.

literal: Day xinhai: attendants were dispatched separately to tour the provinces and commanderies, observe local customs, and inquire into the people's hardships.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day he sent courtiers through the provinces to observe customs and hear the people's grievances.

literal: Day renzi: Wuhui lured and seized Prince of Yiyang Yuan Jie.
idiomatic: On the renzi day Wuhui tricked and captured Yuan Jie, Prince of Yiyang.

literal: Second month, day jisi: an edict that Acting Palace Attendant of Unbroken Communication Xing Ying was to go as envoy to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the jisi day, he ordered Xing Ying, Acting Palace Attendant of Unbroken Communication, as envoy to Liu Yilong.

literal: Five thousand men were levied from Chang'an to dredge Kunming Pool.
idiomatic: Five thousand men were sent from Chang'an to dredge Kunming Pool.

literal: Third month: Jiuquan fell.
idiomatic: In the third month Jiuquan was taken.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengchen: Wuhui raided Zhangye; Tufa Baozhou encamped at Shandan.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the gengchen day, Wuhui attacked Zhangye while Tufa Baozhou camped at Shandan.

literal: Day bingxu: an edict that General Who Pacifies the Army, Prince of Yongchang Jian and others were to command the armies against Baozhou.
idiomatic: On the bingxu day he ordered Jian, Prince of Yongchang, General Who Pacifies the Army, and others to lead the armies against Baozhou.

literal: Fifth month, day xinmao: the imperial carriage traveled to the northern frontier.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the fifth month the emperor went to the northern frontier.

literal: Day yisi: Wuhui again besieged Zhangye but could not take it and withdrew.
idiomatic: On the yisi day Wuhui again besieged Zhangye, failed, and retreated.

literal: Day bingchen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the bingchen day the court returned to the capital.

literal: Sixth month, day dingchou: the imperial grandson Jun was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the sixth month the imperial grandson Jun was born; there was a general amnesty and a new reign title.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage traveled to Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the emperor went to Yinshan.

literal: Day jichou: Prince of Yongchang Jian reached Fanhe, defeated Baozhou, and Baozhou fled.
idiomatic: On the jichou day Jian, Prince of Yongchang, reached Fanhe, broke Baozhou, and Baozhou fled.

literal: Day bingshen: the Empress Dowager, Lady Dou, died at the traveling palace.
idiomatic: On the bingshen day the Empress Dowager, Lady Dou, died at the traveling palace.

literal: Day guichou: Baozhou killed himself; his head was sent to the capital.
idiomatic: On the guichou day Baozhou took his own life and his head was sent to the capital.

literal: Eighth month, day jiashen: Wuhui surrendered and sent Yuan Jie, Prince of Yiyang, and the generals and soldiers.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the jiashen day, Wuhui surrendered and delivered Yuan Jie, Prince of Yiyang, with the officers and troops.

literal: Ninth month, day renyin: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the renyin day, the court returned to the capital.

literal: Winter, eleventh month, day dinghai: the imperial carriage traveled to the north of the mountains.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on the dinghai day, the emperor went north of the mountains.

literal: Twelfth month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: That year fifteen provinces and garrisons suffered famine; granaries were opened for relief.
idiomatic: That year fifteen provinces and garrisons knew famine; the storehouses were opened for relief.

literal: Jie'er, son of Prince of Henan Yao, was made Prince of Hejian, later re-enfeoffed as Prince of Lueyang.
idiomatic: Jie'er, son of Yao, Prince of Henan, was made Prince of Hejian and later Prince of Lueyang.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day guimao: Juqu Wuhui was appointed General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Jiuquan.
idiomatic: In the second year, on the guimao day of the first month of spring, Juqu Wuhui was made General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Jiuquan.

literal: Day jiachen: the imperial carriage traveled to the hot springs.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day the emperor went to the hot springs.

literal: Second month, day renxu: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the renxu day, the court returned to the capital.

literal: Third month, day xinmao: Empress Dowager Hui was buried at Mount Guo.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the xinmao day, Empress Dowager Hui was buried at Mount Guo.

literal: Day gengxu: Prince of Xinxing Jun and Prince of Lueyang Jie'er were guilty and both demoted to duke.
idiomatic: On the gengxu day Jun, Prince of Xinxing, and Jie'er, Prince of Lueyang, were found guilty and both reduced to duke.

literal: Day xinhai: Yujiulü Qieliegui of the Rouran was enfeoffed as King of Shuofang, and Juqu Wannian as King of Zhangye.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day Yujiulü Qieliegui of the Rouran was made King of Shuofang and Juqu Wannian King of Zhangye.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day dingsi: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the dingsi day, Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day gengchen: an edict that General Who Guards the South, Duke of Nanyang Xi Juan, was to campaign against Jiuquan.
idiomatic: On the gengchen day he ordered Xi Juan, Duke of Nanyang, General Who Guards the South, against Jiuquan.

literal: Fifth month, day xinmao: the imperial carriage traveled to the north of the mountains.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the fifth month the emperor went north of the mountains.

literal: Autumn, eighth month, day xinhai: an edict that Palace Attendant Zhang Wei and others were to go as envoys to Liu Yilong.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on the xinhai day, he ordered Zhang Wei, Palace Attendant, and others as envoys to Liu Yilong.

literal: The imperial carriage traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: The emperor went to Hexi.

literal: Ninth month, day wuxu: Prince of Yongchang Jian died.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the wuxu day, Jian, Prince of Yongchang, died.

literal: Winter, eleventh month, day gengzi: General Who Guards the South Xi Juan pacified Jiuquan, capturing Juqu Tianzhou, Zang Jie, and Qu De, with four thousand men and women.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on the gengzi day, Xi Juan pacified Jiuquan and took Juqu Tianzhou, Zang Jie, and Qu De, with four thousand captives.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiaxu: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the jiaxu day, the court returned to the capital.

literal: Day bingwu: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On the bingwu day Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day jiashen: the Emperor came to the Dao altar, received talismans in person, and used the full regalia; banners and flags were all green.
idiomatic: In the third year, on the jiashen day of the first month of spring, the Emperor came to the Dao altar, received talismans in person, and used full regalia with green banners and flags.

literal: The account is in the treatise on Buddhism and Daoism.
idiomatic: The account is in the treatise on Buddhism and Daoism.

literal: Third month, day renyin: Prince of Beiping Changsun Tui was guilty and his noble rank was reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the renyin day, Tui, Prince of Beiping, was found guilty and reduced to marquis.

literal: Summer, fourth month: Wuhui fled across the shifting sands and held Shanshan.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Wuhui fled across the shifting sands and seized Shanshan.

literal: Li Bao's grandson Bao held Dunhuang and sent envoys to submit inward.
idiomatic: Bao, grandson of Li Gao, held Dunhuang and sent envoys to submit.

literal: Fifth month, [1] the imperial carriage traveled to the north of Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, [1] the emperor went north of Yinshan.

literal: Intercalary month: Liu Yilong's General of Dragon Agility Pei Fangming and Inspector of Liangzhou Liu Kangzu invaded Southern Qin; the Southern Qin king Yang Dandang was defeated and fled to Shanggui.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month Pei Fangming, Liu Yilong's General of Dragon Agility, and Liu Kangzu, Inspector of Liangzhou, invaded Southern Qin; Yang Dandang, king of Southern Qin, was beaten and fled to Shanggui.

literal: Sixth month, day bingxu: Dandang attended court at the traveling palace.
idiomatic: On the bingxu day of the sixth month Dandang came to court at the traveling palace.

literal: Earlier a hall had been raised north of Yinshan; when the hall was just completed Dandang arrived, and it was therefore named Broad Virtue.
idiomatic: A hall had already been built north of Yinshan; when it was finished Dandang arrived, and the hall was named Broad Virtue.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day bingyin: an edict that General Who Pacifies the West, Duke of Jianxing Gu Bi, was to command the armies of Longyou and the palace tiger guards, and with Prince of Wudu Yang Baozong and others enter south from Qishan; General Who Conquers the West, Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi, with Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi and others were to command the armies of Guanzhong and enter west from Sanguan—all to meet at Chouchi;
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the bingyin day, he ordered Gu Bi, Duke of Jianxing, General Who Pacifies the West, with the Longyou armies and palace guards and Yang Baozong, Prince of Wudu, south from Qishan; Pi Baozi, Duke of Huaiyang, General Who Conquers the West, with Sima Chuzhi, Prince of Langye, and the Guanzhong armies west from Sanguan—all to join at Chouchi;

literal: Duke of Yulin Sima Wensi was made General Who Conquers the South, advanced to Prince of Qiao, and commanded the military affairs of Luo and Yu, marching south toward Xiangyang;
idiomatic: Sima Wensi, Duke of Yulin, was made General Who Conquers the South, advanced to Prince of Qiao, and commanded Luo and Yu, marching south on Xiangyang;

literal: General Who Conquers the South, Duke of Dong'an Diao Yong, marched east toward Guangling to cut off Fangming's line of retreat.
idiomatic: Diao Yong, Duke of Dong'an, General Who Conquers the South, marched east on Guangling to block Fangming's retreat.

literal: Year 4, spring, first month, day jisi: General Who Conquers the West Pi Baozi and others greatly defeated Liu Yilong's generals at Lexiang, capturing the generals Wang Huanzhi and Wang Changqing; Qiang Xuanming and Xin Bofen abandoned Xiabian and fled, were pursued and beheaded, and all their troops were captured.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the jisi day of the first month of spring, Pi Baozi and the western army routed Liu Yilong's generals at Lexiang, taking Wang Huanzhi and Wang Changqing; Qiang Xuanming and Xin Bofen fled from Xiabian, were run down and killed, and their forces were wholly captured.

literal: Day gengwu: the imperial carriage traveled to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day the emperor went to Zhongshan.

literal: Second month, day bingzi: the imperial carriage reached the south of Mount Heng; an edict ordered the officials to carve stone and inscribe a memorial.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingzi day, the court reached the south of Mount Heng and ordered stone carved with an inscription.

literal: That month Chouchi was taken.
idiomatic: That month Chouchi fell.

literal: Third month, day gengshen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the gengshen day, the court returned to the capital.

literal: Day renxu: the state of Wuluohou sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On the renxu day the state of Wuluohou sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Summer, fourth month: Prince of Wudu Yang Baozong plotted rebellion; the generals seized him and sent him to the capital;
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Yang Baozong, Prince of Wudu, plotted rebellion; the generals seized him and sent him to the capital;

literal: the Di and Qiang again set up Baozong's younger brother Wendé as leader and besieged Chouchi.
idiomatic: the Di and Qiang again made Wendé, Baozong's younger brother, their leader and besieged Chouchi.

literal: Day dingyou: a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day there was a general amnesty.

literal: Day jihai: the imperial carriage traveled to Yinshan.
idiomatic: On the jihai day the emperor went to Yinshan.

literal: Fifth month: General Gu Bi greatly defeated the various Di and lifted the siege of Chouchi.
idiomatic: In the fifth month Gu Bi routed the Di and raised the siege of Chouchi.

literal: Sixth month, day gengyin: an edict said: "We have received Heaven's charge over the people and worry over governing the myriad states, wishing to make every household ample and every person provided for, and to raise ritual and righteousness.
idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the sixth month an edict declared: "We have received Heaven's charge and worry over the myriad realms, wishing every household full and every person provided for, and to raise ritual and righteousness.

literal: Yet governors, defenders, magistrates, and chiefs cannot help Us spread favor and virtue or diligently tend the people's hardships—indeed they seize and plunder their goods and add cruelty on top; this is not how to govern.
idiomatic: Yet governors and magistrates do not help Us spread grace or tend the people's hardships; they seize their goods and add cruelty—this is not governance.

literal: Now We again remit the people's property levies for three years; field tax shall be delivered yearly as usual.
idiomatic: We now remit property levies for three years; field tax shall still be paid yearly as usual.

literal: As for governors and the like, each must exert himself in governance, encourage farming and sericulture, and must not rashly issue levies; the responsible offices shall impeach and not indulge.
idiomatic: Governors must govern diligently, encourage farming, and issue no rash levies; the offices shall impeach and not indulge.

literal: " On guisi a great review was held at the western suburb.
idiomatic: On guisi a great review was held at the western suburb.

literal: Autumn, ninth month, day xinchou: the imperial carriage traveled to the southern desert.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, on the xinchou day, the emperor went to the southern desert.

literal: Day jiachen: baggage was left behind and light horse struck the Rouran; the army was divided into four routes.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day baggage was left behind and light horse struck the Rouran in four columns.

literal: The account is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: General Who Guards the North Feng Da fled into the Rouran.
idiomatic: Feng Da, General Who Guards the North, fled to the Rouran.

literal: Winter, eleventh month: General Pi Baozi and others pursued and defeated Liu Yilong's generals at Zhuoshui.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Pi Baozi and others pursued and defeated Liu Yilong's generals at Zhuoshui.

literal: Day jiazi: the imperial carriage reached Shuofang.
idiomatic: On the jiazi day the court reached Shuofang.

literal: An edict said: "We have received the doubled radiance of Our ancestors' enterprise and think to expand the great foundation and elevate it for ten thousand generations.
idiomatic: An edict declared: "We have received the doubled glory of Our ancestors' foundation and mean to enlarge the great base for ten thousand generations.

literal: From the time We undertook the realm, pacifying violence and removing disorder and sweeping away the disobedient, twenty years have passed.
idiomatic: Since We undertook the realm, pacifying violence and clearing the disobedient, twenty years have passed.

literal: Yin and yang have their return; the four seasons have their succession.
idiomatic: Yin and yang turn back; the four seasons succeed one another.

literal: Entrusting the son and employing the worthy are how one rests; honoring meritorious ministers and planning for long duration—such are the unchanging statutes of antiquity and the present alike.
idiomatic: To entrust the heir and employ the worthy is to rest; to honor meritorious ministers and plan long duration is the unchanging law of antiquity and today alike.

literal: Let the Crown Prince assist in governing the myriad affairs and oversee all departments.
idiomatic: Let the Crown Prince assist in the myriad affairs and oversee all departments.

literal: All Our meritorious ministers, long in toil, shall each return their noble ranks to their estates, attend court when summoned, feast before Us, and discuss the Way and present counsel only—they should not again be burdened with arduous offices.
idiomatic: Our long-serving ministers shall each return to their estates, attend when summoned, feast before Us, and counsel only—they should not again bear heavy office.

literal: Select worthy and outstanding men anew to fill the hundred offices.
idiomatic: Select worthy men anew for the hundred offices.

literal: The responsible offices shall clearly set regulations to match Our mind."
idiomatic: The responsible offices shall set regulations to match Our mind."

literal: Twelfth month, day xinmao: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the xinmao day, the court returned from the northern campaign.

literal: Year 5, spring, first month, day renyin: the Crown Prince first oversaw all departments.
idiomatic: In the fifth year, on the renyin day of the first month of spring, the Crown Prince first oversaw all departments.

literal: Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Yidu Mu Shou; Chancellor of State, Duke of Dongjun Cui Hao; Palace Attendant, Duke of Guangping Zhang Li; Palace Attendant, Duke of Jianxing Gu Bi—all assisted the Crown Prince in deciding ordinary government.
idiomatic: Mu Shou, Prince of Yidu, Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; Cui Hao, Duke of Dongjun, Chancellor of State; Zhang Li, Duke of Guangping, Palace Attendant; and Gu Bi, Duke of Jianxing, Palace Attendant—all assisted the Crown Prince in daily government.

literal: All who submitted memorials addressed themselves as subjects; the ritual for memorials was the same as for formal tables.
idiomatic: All who submitted memorials styled themselves subjects; memorial ritual matched that of formal tables.

literal: Day wushen: an edict said: "The foolish people lack understanding, trust and are deluded by demonic heterodoxy, privately keep masters and shamans, and conceal prognostic texts, yin-yang charts, weft books, and occult arts;
idiomatic: On the wushen day an edict declared: "The foolish lack understanding, trust demonic heterodoxy, keep shamans privately, and hide prognostic texts, yin-yang charts, weft books, and occult arts;

literal: and the Buddhist monks, borrowing the empty fictions of the western barbarians, give rise to demonic harm.
idiomatic: and Buddhist monks, borrowing western fictions, breed demonic harm.

literal: This is not how to unify government and teaching or spread pure virtue through the realm.
idiomatic: This does not unify government and teaching or spread pure virtue through the realm.

literal: From princes and dukes down to commoners, whoever privately keeps Buddhist monks, shamans, or workers in gold, silver, and craft in his household shall send them to the government offices and may not harbor them.
idiomatic: From princes down to commoners, whoever privately keeps monks, shamans, or gold and silver craftsmen must send them to the offices and may not hide them.

literal: The limit is the fifteenth day of the second month this year; after that deadline, if they do not come forth, the shaman or monk dies and the householder's clan is executed.
idiomatic: The deadline is the fifteenth day of the second month this year; after it, shamans and monks die and the householder's clan is executed.

literal: Proclaim this clearly so all may hear and know."
idiomatic: Proclaim this clearly so all may know."

literal: Day gengxu: an edict said: "In recent times military and state affairs have been many and civil teaching has not been proclaimed—this is not how to order customs and show the model to the realm.
idiomatic: On the gengxu day an edict declared: "Lately military affairs have crowded out civil teaching—this does not order customs or show the model to the realm.

literal: Now it is decreed that from princes and dukes down to ministers and grandees, their sons shall all attend the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: Now from princes down to ministers, all sons shall attend the Imperial Academy.

literal: Sons of artisans, craftsmen, stable grooms, and runners shall practice their fathers' and elder brothers' trades and may not privately establish schools.
idiomatic: Sons of artisans, grooms, and runners shall learn their fathers' trades and may not set up private schools.

literal: Violators: the teacher dies and the householder's clan is executed."
idiomatic: Violators: the teacher dies and the householder's clan is executed."

literal: Second month, day xinwei: Prince of Zhongshan Chen and eight other generals, for being late after the northern campaign, were beheaded south of the capital.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the xinwei day, Chen, Prince of Zhongshan, and eight other generals were beheaded south of the capital for lateness after the northern campaign.

literal: Day guiyou: General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Leiping Pi, died.
idiomatic: On the guiyou day Pi, Prince of Leiping, General of Agile Cavalry, died.

literal: Day gengchen: the imperial carriage traveled to Lu
idiomatic: On the gengchen day the imperial carriage traveled to Lu

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: [2] Third month, day wuxu: a great assembly was held at the southern pool of Na.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the wuxu day, [2] a great assembly was held at the southern pool of Na.

literal: Envoys of four missions were sent to the Western Regions.
idiomatic: Envoys of four missions were sent to the Western Regions.
